# The First Echo

Long ago, when the world was newly formed, Sound had no memory. Words spoken would vanish instantly, never to be heard again. This troubled the young goddess Resonara, who loved to sing but grew lonely knowing her songs disappeared forever into the void.

One day, she climbed the highest mountain and sang her most beautiful melody. As the last note faded, she wept, and her tears fell into a deep canyon below. The canyon, moved by her sorrow, caught her song in its stone walls and held it gently.

"Why do you cry?" asked the canyon.

Resonara gasped—she could hear her own melody singing back to her, mixed with the canyon's voice.

"You answered me!" she exclaimed with joy.

"I will always answer," promised the canyon. "I will remember every sound that enters me and send it back to those who need to hear."

Grateful, Resonara blessed the canyon and all its siblings—caves, valleys, and tunnels throughout the world—with the gift of echo. From that day forward, no voice would ever be truly alone, and every sound would find its way back home, even if only as a whisper.

This is why echoes exist: they are the world's promise to remember.

# The First Stars

In the beginning, the world was wrapped in endless twilight—neither dark nor bright, but a grey emptiness that stretched forever. The people wandered without direction, for there was nothing to guide them through the dim expanse.

A young weaver named Aria grew tired of the monotony. She collected the brightest threads she could find—golden strands from summer wheat, silver from winter frost, and brilliant blues from the deepest mountain lakes. Night after night, she wove these threads into a magnificent tapestry, pouring all her hope and longing into each careful stitch.

When she finished, the tapestry blazed with such beauty that it seemed alive. Aria climbed the highest mountain and cast her creation into the sky. The moment it left her hands, the tapestry shattered into countless pieces, each thread transforming into a point of brilliant light.

These became the first stars, scattered across the darkness like jewels on velvet. The grey twilight finally gave way to true night, and the stars provided guidance to all who wandered below.

From that day forward, weavers have been honored among the people, for they remember that even in darkness, beauty and light can be created by patient, hopeful hands.

A young shepherd named Kael refused to accept this emptiness. He wove these together not with thread, but with breath and intention, creating a tapestry of potential sound.

When his work was complete, Kael climbed to where earth met sky and released his creation with a shout—the first voice the world had ever known. The tapestry exploded outward, each fragment finding its voice. Leaves learned to rustle, stones to clatter, water to babble and roar.
